nodes.name: SnO2 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: SnO2 was prepared through hydrothermal method as contrast sample (detailed procedure in Figures S4-S8 of Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: Co3O4 and SnO2 were prepared as contrast samples (Figures S4-S8).

nodes.name: Co3O4 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co3O4 was prepared through hydrothermal method as contrast sample (detailed procedure in Figures S4-S8 of Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: Co3O4 and SnO2 were prepared as contrast samples (Figures S4-S8).

nodes.name: Co3O4/SnO2 Heterostructure Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Two-step hydrothermal synthesis: First SnO2 was prepared as support, then Co3O4 nanosheets were grown interlaced on SnO2 support to create heterogeneous interfaces. SEM, TEM, and elemental line scan confirm SnO2 serves as support for subsequent Co3O4 nanosheet growth without deep burial (Figures S9-S11).

unit_operations.name: Co3O4 Nanosheets Interlaced Growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: subsequent interlaced growth of Co3O4 nanosheets to create many interfaces

nodes.source_text: Co3O4/SnO2 was synthesized through a two-step hydrothermal method. ... SnO2 functions as a support for the subsequent interlaced growth of Co3O4 nanosheets to create many interfaces without being buried deeply below the surface (Figures S9-S11).

nodes.description: Cl-mediated electrosynthesis of cyclohexene oxide (2a) at constant current
nodes.source_text: At a constant current density of 100 mA cm⁻², Co₃O₄/SnO₂ delivers a higher 2a yield, with a potential ∼100 mV lower than that of Co₃O₄... The 2a yield over Co₃O₄/SnO₂ for the first 0.5 h is ∼0.70 mmol and remains at ∼0.55 mmol during prolonged measurements... The scale-up electrosynthesis of 2a (2.74 g) was achieved through 12 h of continuous electrolysis.

Cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves (Figures 3a, S17, and S18) reveal the inertness of SnO₂... The current densities of Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄/SnO₂ vary with increasing potential from ∼1.15 V versus Ag/AgCl.

OER_activity.value: relatively mild with respect to pH

nodes.source_text: The OER activity of Co₃O₄/SnO₂ is relatively mild with respect to pH, suggesting that the LOM is lower than that of Co₃O₄.
The OER activity of Co₃O₄ is correlated with the pH.

nodes.source_text: The observed decreases in the current densities of Co₃O₄/SnO₂ and Co₃O₄... The large decrease in current density over Co₃O₄ indicates a more active LOM over it.

nodes.description: In situ DEMS for OER LOM confirmation
nodes.source_text: In situ ¹⁸O isotope-labeling experiments reveal ³⁴O₂ and ³⁶O₂ signals for both Co₃O₄/SnO₂ and Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images show Co3O4 (220) plane with lattice spacing of 0.283 nm; in Co3O4/SnO2 adjacent to interface decreases to 0.276 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution (HR) TEM image of Co3O4 presents a (220) plane with a lattice spacing of 0.283 nm (Figure 2c). Notably, the lattice spacing of Co3O4 adjacent to the interface decreases to 0.276 nm in Co3O4/SnO2 (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show rightward shift in the peak of Co3O4 (220) plane in Co3O4/SnO2, indicating shortened interplanar spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 2e) reveal a rightward shift in the peak of the Co3O4 (220) plane in Co3O4/SnO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS spectra display a negative shift in the Co-O bond length of Co3O4/SnO2 compared to Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra (Figure 2f) display a negative shift in the Co-O bond length of Co3O4/SnO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of Co3O4/SnO2 show redshift compared to Co3O4, with greater redshift of A1g peak indicating compression at octahedral Co sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The redshift of the Raman bands of Co3O4/SnO2 compared with those of Co3O4 further indicates the compression of the Co-O bond (Figure 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cl 2p XPS shows stable low Cl content for Co3O4/SnO2 at various reaction times; Co3O4 shows drastic increase after 1.5 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) of the electrocatalysts suggests the stable low Cl content of Co3O4/SnO2 at various reaction times (Figure 4a). Conversely, the Cl content over the Co3O4 surface drastically increases after 1.5 h of electrolysis (Figure 4b).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows decreasing A1g peak intensity and redshift for Co3O4 with increasing potential; unchanged A1g peak for Co3O4/SnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With increasing applied potential, the A1g peak intensity of Co3O4 decreases (Figure S31), indicating that more Co-O bonds are broken... In contrast, the unchanged A1g peak of Co3O4/SnO2 (Figure 5b) demonstrates its strong structural stability.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS shows unchanged peaks for Co3O4/SnO2 before/after electrolysis; positive shift for Co3O4 after electrolysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p XPS spectra (Figure 5c) show that the Co 2p peak of Co3O4/SnO2 remains unchanged before and after electrolysis. Conversely, a positive shift is observed after electrolysis of Co3O4.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM, TEM, and elemental line scan reveal SnO2 as support for interlaced growth of Co3O4 nanosheets creating interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and corresponding elemental line scan reveal that SnO2 functions as a support for the subsequent interlaced growth of Co3O4 nanosheets to create many interfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: Similar electrochemical surface areas (ECSAs) for Co3O4 and Co3O4/SnO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the similar electrochemical surface areas (ECSAs) of Co3O4 and Co3O4/SnO2 rule out the contribution of the ECSA to the differences in Cl contents (Figure S29).

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance (Rct) of Co3O4/SnO2 remains unchanged during electrosynthesis; changes for Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Owing to the strong Cl resistance of Co3O4/SnO2, the charge transfer resistance (Rct) ... remain unchanged during the 2a electrosynthesis process (Figures 5e,f, S33, and S34).
